answer: A memory-bound attestation protocol curbs Sybil attacks by requiring agents to traverse large pointer tables initialized from a yarrow entropy pool. Verifiers demand sequential memory lookups that exceed processor cache limits, pushing latency past a strict hardware ledge that cannot be parallelized. An attacker must dedicate scarce physical DRAM bandwidth per persona to survive the verification tide. However, memory bus saturation degrades performance for benign co-hosted agents.
